question.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2\pi x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=2\pi  \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x) & ⇒ & v=-\frac{1}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2\pi x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)\,\text{d}x & =2\pi x\cdot (-\frac{1}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x))-\int (-\frac{1}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x))\cdot 2\pi \,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}2\pi x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)\,\text{d}x & =-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x)\,{|}_{0}^{1}+2{\int }_{0}^{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x)\,{|}_{0}^{1}+\frac{2}{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-2(1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi \cdot 1)-0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi \cdot 0))+\frac{2}{\pi }(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi \cdot 1)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi \cdot 0)) \\  & =-2(-1-0)+\frac{2}{\pi }(0-0) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
